title: onprem: add RKE2+Ubuntu offline bundle + rollback tooling for air-gapped installer
author: Ava Park
description:
Motivation: customers deploying the private installer into air-gapped RKE2 clusters running Ubuntu 22.04 have encountered missing apt packages and incompatible vendored artifacts during upgrades. This PR produces a curated offline bundle for RKE2+Ubuntu, vendors required third-party artifacts (RKE2 images, kernel modules, sysctl configs), and adds a rollback helper to the installer to enable safe downgrade when a node-level upgrade fails.

What this PR does: produces a reproducible offline bundle (tarball + TUF metadata), adds an APT mirror helper for Ubuntu 22.04 packaging, vendors rke2 images and systemd unit patches, updates Helm templates to support the reusable offline bundle layout, and implements a rollback orchestration script plus a controller hook that can trigger an automated rollback on failure. Also adds documentation and test harness for validating bundle integrity in CI.

Checklist: - [x] Generate offline bundle with TUF metadata and manifest - [x] Vendor RKE2 images and containerd/GPU kernel modules - [x] Add apt mirror config and packaging scripts for Ubuntu 22.04 - [x] Helm chart values & templates updated to read from offline bundle - [x] Rollback tooling implemented with integration tests - [x] Add docs and run end-to-end test in perf-canary cluster - [x] Add Linear links and release notes

Testing and validation: end-to-end validation performed on rke2-flatcar and rke2-ubuntu-22.04 clusters in the perf-canary environment, including air-gap install from ISO, bundle apply, upgrade, and forced-failure rollback scenarios. TUF metadata verified and CI gate added to ensure bundle SHA checks pass before publish.

Upgrade/rollback notes: The rollback helper keeps a pre-upgrade snapshot of deployed manifests and container images; invoking the rollback endpoint will restore manifests and reorder node drains to minimize disruption. Operators should ensure the offline bundle contains the previous stable RKE2 image tag to allow rollback.

Backward compatibility: Installer remains backward compatible with existing offline bundles; new fields are optional and documented in the offline-bundles.md.

Related: Linear ENG-2129 (airgap bundle generation), ENG-2214 (rollback orchestration).

vendor/rke2: add rke2 v1.26.4+rdw-1 images and sha manifests
packaging/apt: add ubuntu-22.04 mirror helper and apt-repo metadata
installer/helm: read offline bundle layout + optional apt mirror settings
tooling/rollback: add rollback controller + orchestration script
ci: add e2e airgap canary job and bundle sha check
review_thread: Miguel Santos: Please add TUF metadata verification to the CI pipeline so we don't accidentally publish malformed bundles.
Ava Park: Added jest-like TUF verification step to ci/pipelines/e2e-airgap.yml; it verifies root and snapshot signatures before publish.
Priya Nair: Can we reduce bundle size by excluding debug binaries? Also suggest adding a size report to the build artifact.
Ava Park: Excluded debug artifacts and added bundle-size.txt artifact output with a threshold check. See generate-offline-bundle.sh commit.
Ben Thompson: Approving after CI pass. One nit: document rollback preconditions more explicitly.
Ava Park: Expanded rollback-runbook.md with network/preflight checks and example curl calls to the rollback endpoint.
release_notes: Add RKE2+Ubuntu 22.04 offline bundle support and rollback tooling for the on-prem air-gapped installer; includes vendored RKE2 images and APT mirror helper. Operators should include previous stable image tags in bundles to enable rollback.
testing_instructions: 1) run scripts/generate-offline-bundle.sh --target rke2-ubuntu-22.04 --output /tmp/bundle.tar.gz 2) upload bundle to testmirror and update installer values.yaml offlineBundle.url 3) deploy charts/private-installer with helm --set offlineBundle.enabled=true 4) simulate a failed upgrade by corrupting a node image and trigger rollback via tooling/rollback/ctl rollback --cluster <id>
notes: This PR contains vendored third-party artifacts; follow internal licensing checklist before publishing the bundle to customer-facing registries.
